newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche says currencies had favourable effects.
newsitem.headline: Roche says currencies had favourable effects.

text.p: Roche Holding AG said the overall positive movement of exchange rates in the first half of 1996 had a favourable effect on the group's financial condition and results.

Roche said in its six month report that the trend of an appreciating Swiss franc during 1994/95 was reversed in the first half of 1996, and by the end of June all major foreign currencies traded at higher rates against the Swiss franc compared with the end of 1995.
For Roche the most important currency is the U.S. dollar and both operating assets and sales in the United States represent close to 40 percent of wordwide sales.
At the start of 1994 the dollar had been trading at 1.48 francs, but fell to 1.15 francs at the end of 1995.
But by the end of June the dollar had increased by two percent to the franc compared with June, 1995.
Roche's operating profit in the first half rose eight percent to 1.93 billion Swiss francs.

Roche's non-operating income, essentially the result of its financial operations, rose by 31 percent to 786 million Swiss francs in the first half, with the increase partially due to higher currency exchange rates, Roche said.
